newsitem.title: ITALY: BancoNapoli trims losses in 1st half 1996.
newsitem.headline: BancoNapoli trims losses in 1st half 1996.

text.p: Troubled Banco di Napoli said it posted a first half 1996 loss of 674.7 billion lire against a loss of 1.56 trillion lire in the first six months of 1995.
The bank made losses of 3.16 trillion lire in the full 1995 year, the biggest in Italian banking history.
In the first quarter of this year, the bank posted a loss of 286.3 billion lire.

The bank said in a statement issued after a board meeting that customer loans at end-June totalled 41.94 trillion lire, 21.1 percent down on the same 1995 period, while deposits were 23.44 trillion, down 0.5 percent.

The bank's first half net interest income was 850.4 billion lire, down 22.4 percent, with operating income of 1.156 trillion lire, down 9.2 percent. Gross operating profit was 78.2 billion lire, down 57.9 percent.

The bank's two trillion lire capital increase, as part of a rescue plan, got under way earlier this month and will run until October 8. The government is underwriting the cash call and has said it will set up a rump company to take over much of the bank's hefty bad debt portfolio.

The bank's statement said net bad debts at the end of June this year totalled 4.887 trillion lire, an increase of 44.7 percent on the same period last year. The ratio of bad debts to loans was 11.7 percent.
Accounting adjustments and provisions totalled 816.2 billion lire.

The bank said the first half results were affected by the provisions for problem credits, by the weakness of the bank's assets and the high volume of non-performing activities. But the bank said its financial position was showing signs of gradual improvement after heavy losses in the last two years.

"The recapitalisation just started, the more careful management of financial and credit flows and the holding down of costs should have a positive influence on future economic results, accelerating the recovery of the bank," it said.
